title: Microorganisms
examples: What is the difference between bacteria and fungi?
Can microorganisms be good or bad?
What are some examples of protists?

explain.say: Today we are learning about microorganisms. These are tiny living things you cannot see easily.

items: We need tools to see them.

explain.say: Bacteria are single-celled living organisms. They reproduce very quickly using simple division.
Fungi are also microorganisms, but they are not bacteria. They often get nutrients from decaying matter.
Protists are a diverse group of eukaryotes. They can move and feed in various ways in water.
Microbes can be useful in many ways. For example, some bacteria help us digest our food.
However, some microbes can also be harmful. For example, some bacteria can cause infections in humans.

faq.q: Are all microorganisms harmful to humans?
faq.a: No, many microorganisms are helpful. Some bacteria, for instance, are essential for digestion.

faq.q: How are protists different from bacteria?
faq.a: Protists have more complex structures than bacteria. Bacteria are much simpler, single-celled organisms.
asks: What is the difference between protists and bacteria?

faq.q: What is the main difference between fungi and plants?
faq.a: Fungi get their food from dead or decaying matter. Plants, however, make their own food using sunlight.
No, most bacteria are harmless or even helpful. Only specific types can cause infections.
Protists are most commonly found in wet environments. They are often found living in freshwater or marine settings.

facts: Bacteria are prokaryotic, meaning they lack a nucleus.
Fungi obtain nutrients by absorbing them from their surroundings.
Protists are a very diverse group that includes some plant-like and animal-like organisms.
Some beneficial bacteria are used in making yogurt and cheese.

quiz.say: Which group includes yeast and mould?
quiz.show: Yeast and mould belong to which group?
quiz.why: Fungi are organisms like yeast and mould that grow on decaying matter.

wrong.1: Bacteria are single-celled organisms, but yeast is more complex.
wrong.2: Protists are usually found in water and are not typically yeasts.
wrong.3: Fungi are not animals, even though they can sometimes be eaten.

quiz.say: Which microbe group is known for helping in digestion?
quiz.why: Specific bacteria live in our gut and help us break down food.

wrong.0: Protists are generally found in aquatic environments, not inside us.
wrong.1: Viruses are not considered living organisms in the same way as these three groups.
wrong.3: While fungi decompose things, bacteria are the main gut helpers.

quiz.say: A single-celled organism that moves using pseudopods is likely a:
quiz.why: Amoeba, a type of protist, moves using temporary extensions called pseudopods.

wrong.0: Plants are multicellular and do not move like this.
wrong.2: Bacteria usually move using flagella or simple sliding.
wrong.3: Fungi generally grow by spreading spores, not by moving themselves.
